tips.comment: PARTISAN HERO should take all the beating here as 2/1 market leader. Rare Change carries a poor FlatStats rating alongside F Marsh’s 5% SR (A/E 0.19) with fancied runners on Sundays and R Hughes’ 13% SR (A/E 0.46) with fancied runners on Sundays also, meanwhile the E Bethell yard are struggling of late (8% SR, A/E 0.57 over the past fortnight) along with C Rodriguez (1/27, A/E 0.2) which puts me off Native Instinct. The rest are all poorly FS rated and some carry negative stats too, making this much easier for the jolly. With a top + blue FS rating, the son of Muhaarar has looked incredibly progressive since switching to the D Loughnane yard; winning on three occasions and placing on his six other starts. He won LTO at Epsom, albeit by a head, but is running off just a 3lb higher mark today and dropping class to make life easier. The 5yo isn't guaranteed to get a freebie out in front due to NI, but he’ll be thereabouts, the yard are in form (15% SR, A/E 1.67 over the past month) and R Ryan brings a 47% SR (A/E 1.43) on favourites from the West Midlands.

Rare Change is trained by Richard Hughes. This gelding by Mehmas has better chances to return to winning ways now dropped in class. Last run was in Cl2 Hc at Goodwood. Now in this Cl3 Hc contest, he can make the frame under Finley Marsh. The trainer-jockey combo has a 17% win rate (+14 LSP) this year.

This horse looks well worth a bet dropping back in trip here. Clearly loves this ground and looks to have the pace (and the handicap mark) to be competitive here. The trainer is one of the best at racing here horses off winnable marks and the horse looks well worth am e/w bet.

Callum Rodriguez's return to the saddle is a plus. Was quite unsettled on seasonal debut last time out but should come on for the run. Trainer goes well with his 3 year old handicappers at Pontefract. Well bred, well drawn, just squeaks an each way bet.

I'm a tad concerned about the draw here and feel as though the selection needs to get out of the traps into a good position. Having said that, the horse's stats are deceptively good and if the favourite doesn;t fire we have an underrated bet

Impressed when winning in this class on return over 5f @ Beverley and ran much better than form figure would indicate Lto in a hot class 4 over 6f @ York, as blindfold came off late when stalls opened. Has plum draw here, retains a decent mark of 81 and very good jockey/trainer combination, makes current 12/1 solid Ew value here.

The outsider of the field, and Michael Appleby has dropped him into a class three handicap after finishing unplaced at Epsom with the last outing. This track could be more suitable with rising ground to the winning line, proving his stamina ability to stay on at the business end.

Favourite is a C&D winner but looks on a stiff enough mark and will struggle to give this strong stayer the weight. Has caught the eye a couple of times including here at Pontefract when just denied over a trip just shy of this one. Good apprentice booked who has ridden a few winners and plenty of places from his last dozen rides. Can improve again with a stiffer test and though does find it hard to win looks ready to strike off this mark with a valuable 7lb off from good claimer. Big chance.

Almudena made a big improvement when stepping up to 2 mile at the end of last term and has had a down the pack run on the return on the AW at the start of this month and will be all the better for that run, with a return to turf today and a step up in trip to 2m2f likely to suit
Slowly away when scored by 1/2l off 72 over 2m at Kempton three starts back; fifth beaten 4l off 74 last time; up in trip; returns to turf after AW spell; the pick on balance of form
Won over course and distance on the 8th of April and will welcome the step up in trip following 2 runs over 2 miles.

Preference here goes to the O Greenall & J Guerriero trained, El Borracho. Comfortably held at Doncaster on his latest outing over fences. Makes the switch back to the flat having been away for a lengthy period of time. Obviously the stable thought best to give him a break. Returns on a fair mark if he can replicate his runner-up finish at this course in 2023. Looks competitive on the figures. Aiden Brookes claims a valuable 3lb that leaves this horse well treated off his peak form.

Adoria Of Achill was unplaced in 3 starts as a juvenile but has improved for handicapping this year. 4th of 12 at Nottingham in April she then won at Haydock by 1.5 lengths last month. A 5lbs rise looks fair and she can go in again

Style of Life seems to be the likely front runner in this contest and did that to good effect last time setting the pace before quickening up under this jockey. A repeat of these tactics should yield the same result here.

Race 7 at Pontefract today is the Napoleons Bradford Handicap (Class 5) for 3 year olds and upwards over 1,615 m and the suggested wager is for the each way on the 5yo gelding Mount King from the Tim Easterby yard and will be ridden by David Allan , this son of National Defense is in reasonably good form at present and is down in class from his latest decent effort , has a top chance of landing the spoils here and must not be ignored

Six career runs for the 3yo filly, quite consistent. Just two starts this year, 4th last time out on her handicap debut, getting going too late that day, but it was a much stronger looking contest than this race today. She was a good maiden winner during April. She’ll be fresh after a 5 week break, suited by the quick and is open to more improvement.

Moonbow has won a point and a bumper and although beaten a long way he did not do too badly in his first hurdle race as his progress was halted by a mistake two out after which he weakened to be 3rd of 8 to Emily Love beaten 28 lengths at Perth he would not want too much rain at Hexham as he was very disappointing on good to soft at Ayr in a decent bumper.
Maggie's Boy finished second at Cartmel & more recently finished third at Southwell having ran well. Maggie's Boy will be wearing a tongue tie for the first time today which should keep him sharp.

Clearly, Joel Parkinson and Sue Smith have worked diligently with this 5-year-old, as he hinted at his potential by finishing a commendable 3rd in this novice race at Bangor 16 days ago. With the increase in distance, he can certainly build on this performance, making an attractive bet each-way at 20/1.
Keen, travelled, readily, improved on chase debut landing a handicap by 3 1/2l off 92 here last time; sound surface suits; more to come; threat

And my second tip of this race is Royal Deeside who well over course and distance last time out. Harry Reed on board again. He beat the in form 'Am Still Here' marginally but those two were miles clear of the rest.

The model I run suggests High Moon can win this one. High Moon lines up here with the second highest RPR of the 8 runner field and has the highest official ranking. Is not overly penalised for it int he weights and comes here with some reasonable form. Figures of 53-32 shows some improvement and consistency, so hopefully this is the race for High MOon to get overly the line in first. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
I'm going to have two swings at this race at Hexham, firstly Fortunate Fella who plugged on gamely to grind a result at Fontwell last time out.

O'Faolain's Glory jumped well on first two chase starts (1st and 3rd) showing a real aptitude for the game. Fell at the 1st on next chase start and then 6 of next 7 runs were over hurdles. Did not show much until last time when 2nd in a class 2 hurdle from well out the handicap. With confidence seemingly now well restored he goes back to chasing and if he holds form from that last run over these bigger obstacle today this race presents a winning opportunity and he should go close.

Interesting they are reverting to fences here, as last chase run resulted in a win 5 runs back over 2.4 miles @ Worcester and only 1lb higher here. Good owner/trainer does well when riding his horses and takes off valuable 7lb, making current 10/1 solid Ew value here.
Less Legacy is dropped back in distance today and runs well at Hexham. Should run well and has a good chance.

The model I run has suggested outsider, Tommie Gun, as the value bet in the final race of the day. Tommie Gun lines up here with by far the highest RPR of the 6 runners, but is only second lowest official rating. This leaves him looking very attractive at this mark and if able to put a good run and jumping together, might be ahead of the rest of this field. Big price relates to being pulled in the last 3 races and reliability. Has had a break and some time to rest since then, but goes out here with new connections and looking to make an impact. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0,5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Kow Boy Sivola has had two runs since a 217 day break and should be fully fit now for this step up in trip today on handicap debut. Went well for a long way here last time and after going wide on the home bend was not given a vigorous ride by his jockey. Likely to be asked more of today and with all conditions suitable and Hughes in the saddle the race presents an opportunity.
Jakama looks set to run well in the finale at Hexham at a big price. The mare won twice last season and can strike again today for her new yard.

Hunky Dory has shown decent form overall without actually winning. He drops from a 0-80 grade handicap to a 0-72 and is dropped one pound by the handicapper. At York last time, Hunky Dory had a whole load of things go wrong. In early trouble, switched late on, and then denied a run, we can put a line through that, and he is better than that. After that, Hollie Doyle has been replaced by George Downing. Yard in good form. Good opportunity.

Trainer has a strike rate of 35% here over the last 5 year and the jockey 25% over the last 12 months. This girl ran well from an unfavoured draw at Chester on her seasonal return last month, and whilst hampered in running finished strongly. Hunky Dory is too short to consider and Key Witness unproven on turf which leads me to this lass, I wouldn't take any less than 4s though.

I noticed this one has been tipped on the Sporting Life homepage, but he's not been supported much today, which is a positive for value seekers. The yard is going great guns, and I'm sure this gelding can improve enough on his Goodwood run to take a hand in this.

Sustained is really overpriced here, being dropped back to 7f cheek pieces on first time I think this will enable a lot for this horse, playing it safe each way but this horse will definitely outrun its odds.
Key Witness showed much improvement to see off a field of ten at Chelmsford two months ago. Should go well on handicap debut.

6 year old gelding Sired by Aclaim is 1 from 1 over course and distance. That was on soft ground and that does seem to be his preference. There is rain in the forcast so if it arrives soon enough it will enhance his chances. Decent apprentice Jockey takes off 7lb (from 10-0) and horse seems to be happy carrying weight anyway. At 12-1 I'm happy to take the chance but will go small each way today.

She is coming here in very good form (151) and versatile and excels on softer ground. It is also worth noting that she has won off a higher mark in the past but will need to continue to improve since going up in class.

Definite signs of ability in their 3 non handicap runs to date, including good effort on 3yo return. Goes in first time handicap here off reasonable mark of 72, today's pilot showed their worth @ Royal Ascot this week and very good trainer is now coming into form after a quiet spell, making current 16/1 very good Ew value in the race.
Cornish storm is the one to beat my NAP was unfortunate in running lto was forced wide back in a smaller field I think if this horse has kept the form will be difficult to beat this one

Good trainer and a jockey, who knows this course well, combine their talents here with Run Of Luck, who performs much betetr on turf than the synthetics he's been tried on from time to time. Won fresh-up in this prep and I have a sneaking suspicion that probably took the deg off for his next run on Tapeta anyway and the trqack didn't look to suit anyweay, so that run is probably best forgiven. Produced a betetr effort for fifth last time out when returned to the turf and likely to go on with it now.
Three Yorkshiremen is well treated in this grade, proven in cheekpieces, and has strong Class 6 form. Sean Levey won on him 11 days ago and retains the ride.

YQUEM has to be of interest for an Irish yard who have had a couple run fine races this month including a win and a sound effort in deep company at Ascot. That likely advertises the wellbeing of the yard's small string and in this basement grade this filly sent over making handicap debut looks interesting.

Decent AW form from the 6yo this spring and a nice run on his return to turf two weeks ago, over this 8f trip. He was a close 3rd of 9 that day, the rest well beaten, and he didn’t have a clear passage. Something to build on, suited by the slower ground and this is a very weak looking handicap.

A long time maiden , over 20 races , but he showed a lot of promise to finish second over 2 furlongs longer than todays trip at wolverhampton two weeks ago. I'm tipping that he can break is duck today over a shorter trip 7 furlongs . He looks to have a nice draw.
Scenario is lightly raced and open to improvement. Ran well to finish 4th st Brighton earlier this month. Got centrepiece on for the first time today and that can help.

Rival is in stall number 6 which is fine for his usual running style sitting just off the pace, and the race should be run at a fair tempo. He finished sixth 15 days ago at Chepstow and needed the outing after a break, and now fitted with first time blinkers. His mark of 52 is very workable based on past form, especially as he is a course and distance winner and has gone well on this ground. Trained by John Flint and ridden by Callum Hutchinson, he has had 43 runs with 2 wins and 6 places giving a 5% win rate and 14% place rate. With fitness on his side now and blinkers added, he looks like a solid each way chance in a winnable race to me

With exception of effort @ Wolverhampton 3 runs back, has been running with merit Turf/Aw of late and retains a decent mark of 46 here. Good pilot retains ride and very shrewd trainer likes to have winners @ one of this local tracks, making current 18/1 decent Ew value here.

ALMIZAN has been placed in one race from six starts third over 1m at Chelmsford City on her latest outing earlier this month course distance and goinf should suit seems well treated and could well be able to win this race
